Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Full-thickness chondrosis at the proximal tibiofibular joint with marginal osteophytes and subchondral cystic change and intra-osseous ganglion cyst formation. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. Small multilobulated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Extensive complex tear at the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with maceration and extrusion. Reactive edema at the joint line.
Medial compartment cartilage: Full thickness cartilage denudation throughout the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau with subchondral cystic change and marrow edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the anterior weightbearing surfaces. High grade chondrosis along the peripheral lateral joint. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the medial trochlea. High-grade fissuring at the median ridge with likely an early delaminating component extending along the medial patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal fibers with bowing related to medial meniscus extrusion.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Mild popliteus tendonesis without tear. Ganglion cyst about the myotendinous junction. 

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild proximal patellar tendinosis without tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 4 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Extensive complex tear at the body and posterior horn of medial meniscus with maceration and extrusion of the body.
2.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, severe in the medial compartment. 
3.	Mild proximal patellar tendinosis without tear.
4.	Mild popliteus tendonesis without tear.

Central supporting system 
  Normal orientation with intact ligament fiber of ACL and PCL. 
  No anterior tibial translation is observed.  
  
 Medial compartment  
  Focal mild hyperintense fissuring articular cartilage at weight bearing part, mid medial femoral condyle,  without subchondral bone lesion.  
  Medial meniscus is not torn..  
  Medial collateral ligament is preserved.  
  
 Lateral compartment  
  Diffuse degenerative thinning articular cartilage along the lateral femoral condyle and tibial plateau 
     is observed. No subchondral bone lesion is detected.  
   Marginal osteophytes along the lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau are observed.  
  FCL, popliteus and biceps femoris tendons are intact.   Popliteofibular ligament is preserved. 
   Lateral meniscus is not torn.  
  
 Extensor Mechanism and PF joint 
  Patellofemoral joint is intact.  
  Thickened medial synovial plica is observed.  
  Quadriceps and patellar tendon are preserved.  
  Medial and lateral patellofemoral retinaculum are preserved.  
   Minimal PF joint effusion is observed. 
  
  Few reactive popliteal lymph nodes, measuring upto 7mm. in short axis, are seen.  Thickened medial synovial plica noted.  
  Chondrosis at the mid medial femoral condyle, (grade 2 chondropathy) 
    Degenerative chondrosis at the lateral tibiofemoral joint, marginal osteophytes; 
    OA knee observed.  
   No definite meniscal tear detected.

MRI of left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, AX T2W FS, CO T2W FS

> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, and unclear contour of meniscal root, in favor of tear.
> The contour of PCL is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of tear.
> Enlarged size of ACL and increased interstitial signal intensity on F/S T2WI and mild laxity contour , R/O mucoid degeneration or grade 1 injury.
Joint effusion with mildly increased signal on T1WI and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; in favor of severe hypertrophy of the synovium of right knee, indicative of severe synovitis.
> Loculated fluid with isointensity to muscle on T1WI and hyperintensity on F/S T2WI over anterior lateral aspect of left knee, in favor of residual subcutaneous hematoma.
> Mottled mild hyperintensity foci in proximal tibia ( major at tibial tuberosity) and distal femur and fibula, which shows low signal intensity on T1WI and high signal intensity on T2WI, in favor of residural red bone marrow.
> Increased singal intensity of patellar cartilage with deep fissures, in favor of grade III patellar chondromalacia.
  Wearing of articular cartilage of femoral trochela with subchondral edema and cyst.

Impression: 
1. Tear of posterior horn of left medial meniscus.
2. PCL tear.
3. Grade 1 injury of ACL.
4. Synovitis of left knee joint with suprapetellar bursitis.
5. Subcutaneous edema in left anterior knee with residual subcutaneous hematoma in left lateral knee.
6. Osteoarthritis of left knee with grade 3-4 chondromalacia of patellofemoral joint.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation
